panels.title: Where agent time goes (tool and API durations)
Tool time by tool (range, hours)
panels.description: Host sessions on the runtime hosts (acer-swift, msi-ms7758, asus-b460m) send no events by design: modules/roles/runtime-host.nix sets sam.claude.telemetry off there. Their dev-environment guests do, shown as host/worker; lenovo's host sessions do too. Sum of tool_result duration_ms per tool. An Agent call returns as soon as its subagent starts in the background (about 5 ms), so a subagent's work shows only as its own API and tool events, not as Agent time. Waiting on the human, and idle time between turns, are not tool time. This is summed call time, not wall clock: parallel calls each count in full, and a backgrounded Bash returns at once.

panels.title: Agent time per day by host / worker: tools and API requests (hours)
panels.description: Host sessions on the runtime hosts (acer-swift, msi-ms7758, asus-b460m) send no events by design: modules/roles/runtime-host.nix sets sam.claude.telemetry off there. Their dev-environment guests do, shown as host/worker; lenovo's host sessions do too. Tool time is tool_result duration_ms; API time is api_request duration_ms (model latency, streaming included). Both are summed per day; a day's total can exceed 24 h: parallel sessions and parallel calls each count in full.

targets.expr: sum by (hw) (sum_over_time({observer="harness",event_name="tool_result",host_name=~"$host"} | json attributes_duration_ms="attributes.duration_ms", attributes_worker="attributes.worker" | label_format hw=`{{ .host_name }}/{{ or .attributes_worker "host" }}` | unwrap attributes_duration_ms | __error__="" [$__interval])) / 3600000

sum by (hw) (sum_over_time({observer="harness",event_name="api_request",host_name=~"$host"} | json attributes_duration_ms="attributes.duration_ms", attributes_worker="attributes.worker" | label_format hw=`{{ .host_name }}/{{ or .attributes_worker "host" }}` | unwrap attributes_duration_ms | __error__="" [$__interval])) / 3600000

panels.description: Host sessions on the runtime hosts (acer-swift, msi-ms7758, asus-b460m) send no events by design: modules/roles/runtime-host.nix sets sam.claude.telemetry off there. Their dev-environment guests do, shown as host/worker; lenovo's host sessions do too. A rising p95 for Bash usually means gates, builds or sleeps inside agent commands; for Agent, longer subagents.
